chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me, who said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf from Muhammad ibn Bukayr from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

One who says, when taking his bed, three times: 'Al-hamdu lillahi alladhi 'ala fa-qahara, and al-hamdu lillahi alladhi batana fa-khabara, and al-hamdu lillahi alladhi malaka fa-qadara, and al-hamdu lillahi alladhi yuhyi al-mawta wa yumitu al-ahya', wa huwa 'ala kulli shay'in qadir' — he will emerge from sins as he was on the day his mother gave birth to him.

key_terms.بَطَنَ فَخَبَرَ: He was inward and knew (the secrets)
key_terms.یُحْیِی الْمَوْتَی: He gives life to the dead
key_terms.یُمِیتُ الْأَحْیَاءَ: He causes the living to die

ai.seo_question: What is the supplication for forgiveness of sins before sleeping?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-Amal*, this hadith highlights the spiritual discipline of evening remembrance, linking the physical act of lying down with the soul’s return to its primordial purity. By affirming God’s absolute dominion over elevation, subjugation, and the transition between life and death, the supplication serves as a means of *tazkiyah* (purification), erasing sins to restore the believer to the sinless state of *fitrah* upon waking.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. It was narrated to me by Muhammad b. al-Hassan who said it was narrated to me by Muhammad b. al-Hassan al-Saffar from al-Abbas b. Ma’ruf from Muhammad b. Bukayr from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said: “

One who recites Alh’amdulillaahilladhee a’laa faqahara walh’amdu lillaahilladhee bat’ana fakhabara wal h’amdulillaahilladhee malaka faqadara wal h’amdulillaahilladhee yuh’yil mautaa wa yumeetul ah’yaa-u wa huwa a’laa kulli shai-in Qadeer thrice before going to bed will become as pure as a newborn baby.”
